title: Vera Rubin telescope to remove classified satellites from its data

as_told.title: Pentagon review of Vera Rubin Observatory imagery
as_told.place_text: Vera Rubin Observatory; secure facility in California

plain: The Vera Rubin Observatory, a large new telescope built to survey the whole sky, will scrub classified satellites and other objects from the images it releases, according to two tellers on the show. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel relays this as something she was told, saying the telescope 'is going to remove a lot of classified satellites and other objects.' Michels repeats the claim on a later episode in a stronger form, citing an article in The Atlantic. He says 'all of Rubin's imagery has to be approved by the Pentagon,' and that this review happens at a secure facility in California. Villarroel speaks of objects being removed, while Michels speaks of Pentagon sign-off on everything. If true, it would mean the public's newest view of the sky is filtered before anyone outside the military sees it, and that unexplained objects could be filtered out along with the secret satellites.
